the role of religious coping in the context of localized prostate cancer is complex.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients who experience an increase in their spiritual and religious practices after diagnosis of prostate cancer may experience a reduction in their cancer-related worries.
the majority of prostate cancer patients report a diagnosis-related decrease in daily religious and spiritual practices and experiences.
the role of religion/spirituality in the lives of prostate cancer patients is important and that there may be a need for further research on the role of religion and spirituality in prostate cancer.

there is no evidence that daily religious and spiritual practices are beneficial for prostate cancer patients, and that the development of spiritual/religious interventions for prostate cancer patients is premature.
